acceptanceCriteria: `cem verify` reports `held` only after its own re-execution observes a classified failure of a named test with the hunk reverted; two fixtures (revert breaks compilation; the test also fails without the revert) yield `not-run`.
The dogfood producer offers a cite-the-guarding-test step and the next 30 dogfood changes record the held share in a build-log entry against K1.
Non-Go runners are recorded as limits in the release notes; no runner is reported qualified by this ticket.
body: Source: decision 0523 (docs/decisions/0523-cem-1-0-rc3-verifier-computed-support-2026-10-11.md) and build-log docs/build-log/2026-10-11-cem-1-0-expert-panel.md, origin/main fb11b2274. Proposed CEM-V1-068 and CEM-V1-069. A supported basis may name test IDs; the consumer reverse-applies that one hunk at target and runs only those tests under the fixed go-test runner profile. `held` requires a classified test failure the consumer itself observed; compile, skip or infrastructure failure is `not-run`; a producer-written witness never counts. Today 0 of 8,008 supported non-test Go hunks cite a _test.go file and TCQ-V0-057 selects only hunks that already cite one, so the producer needs a cite-the-guarding-test step or the tier never fires. Every runner other than go test is a recorded limit. Kill criteria K1 (fewer than 25% held over the next 30 dogfood changes drops the headline), K3 (audited held witnesses) and K5 (latency).
title: cem/1.0 P2: hunk-revert falsifier `held` for `go test`, and a producer step that cites the guarding test
